chapter_summary: A passing scent turns a brief encounter into a meditation on how the senses keep what the eye loses. Debolina recognizes that observation must not become possession.

spatality.place: a lane in Mandawa, the wall's scaffolding just behind the speaker
spatality.route: a passer-by crosses the lane and is gone before the next line
spatality.texture: warm air, dust lifting, a scent that arrives before the person does

poetic_parameters.movement: Sufism — seeking union through ecstatic love, here turned toward a scent that will not stay.
writing_skills: sensuous cataloguing that keeps to one sense
anaphora building until the list becomes a lament
a turn from appetite to restraint
poetic_parameters.image_seed: a musk that reaches the scaffold before the man who wears it turns the corner
poetic_parameters.volta: from wanting to keep the scent to refusing to keep the man
poetic_parameters.sonic_texture: long open vowels in air, lane, and name, closing on clipped consonants
poetic_parameters.line_gesture: long enjambed lines that gather speed, then one short line that stops the poem
poetic_parameters.variety_note: The previous poem emptied the street; this one fills it with a single passing body and then has to give that body back.
poetic_parameters.metaphor_family: scent as temporary architecture — doorway, lintel, air that holds a shape and loses it
poetic_parameters.address: the scent first, then the self, in a correction
poetic_parameters.closing_move: the image withdrawn — the lane returned to being only a lane
